settings.name_in_paper: Quantum Best Arm Identification (quantum agent and quantum environment)
unmapped: Quantum access model: the agent queries the environment in superposition via unitary oracles O_e (preparing sum_y sqrt(nu_x(y))|y>) and O_f (phase oracle on reward f(x,y) in {0,1}); 'rounds' are oracle applications, not classical samples
Choosing the number of rounds n ≈ (pi/4) sqrt(1/p) requires knowing p = sum_x |<x|A|0>|^2 a_x
settings.definition_quote: we define a composite Hilbert space $\Hi = \Hi_X\otimes\Hi_Y$ ... \forall x \in X, O_e\ket{x 0} = \ket{x \psi_x} : \abs{\braket{y}{\psi_x}}^2 = \nu_x(y) ... O_f\ket{xy} = -\ket{x y} if f(x,y) = 1, \ket{x y} otherwise.

algorithms.name: QBAI (Quantum Best Arm Identification)
requires_knowledge_of: p (average success probability under A) to set the number of rounds

symbols.w_star: |<x*|A|0>|^2, initial amplitude-squared of the optimal action under the agent's preparation unitary A
symbols.p: sin(theta)^2 = sum_x |<x|A|0>|^2 a_x, initial probability of measuring a rewarding state
symbols.n: number of applications of the Grover-type operator G

conditions: quantum oracle access to environment via O_e and O_f

source.label: th:main_theorem
source.quote: The probability $P_{n}(\tilde x)$ that QBAI will recommend the optimal action $\tilde x$ is maximized when $n \approx \frac{\pi}{4}\sqrt{1/p} - \frac{1}{2}$. It follows that {$P_{n}(\tilde x ) = \abs{\bra{\tilde x }A\ket{0}}^2\frac{a^*}{p}$}.

results.notes: Result gives the (maximal) probability of recommending the optimal arm, not a regret/error bound; recorded as quantity 'other'. With uniform A, success probability is a*/(N E_X[a_x]) after about (pi/4)/sqrt(E_X[a_x]) rounds (paper's discussion, not a separate formal statement). Quantum oracle model, not directly comparable to classical sample complexity.
